_comment: What `layout/power/run_power.py` runs and what it asserts. Everything
in this file that is not a layer number or a PDK constant is an
ASSUMPTION -- where the supply is landed, which resistance corner, what
each sub-block draws -- and it lives here, named and sourced, rather
than inside `adc_block.power-spec.json`, which is geometry and PDK
numbers only. `run_power.py` composes the two into the spec it actually
runs and commits that composed spec beside the report.
`expect` is asserted field by field; a field absent from an `expect`
block is not checked, a field present and wrong fails the run with a
named mismatch. Every float is compared to a round-off tolerance (1e-6
relative, with a 1e-9 absolute floor only so a quantity that is exactly
zero by construction does not demand bit equality). That is six orders
looser than the solver's own 1e-12 achieved residual and many orders
tighter than anything that could change a verdict.
`expect.nets.<net>.droop_sum_mv` and `.abs_current_sum_a` are
aggregates over the WHOLE solved field. Without them `--verify` would
assert ~9 of 870 node voltages and an edit to any of the other 861
would go uncaught -- which is exactly what a tamper test of an earlier
draft of this file found. A sum moves for any single-value edit and,
unlike a checksum, still compares with a tolerance.
`layout_sha256` pins the geometry every case is run against, so a droop
verdict can never silently belong to a different GDS than the one this
repo committed. Same value `layout/erc/cases.json` and
`signoff/gf180-sar-adc.manifest.json` pin.
SITES -- the four places this block's supply is reachable
`ADC_BLOCK` has no supply pad. It has EIGHT label texts on Metal1_Label
34/10 -- one `vdd` and one `vss` in each of four sub-blocks -- and that
is the whole of its declared supply interface. The coordinates below
are those label positions, read out of `layout/adc-top/adc_block.gds`
itself (`klayout.db`, top cell ADC_BLOCK, layer 34/10, text string
matched exactly), and each was mapped to its sub-block by the
instance bounding boxes of the same top cell.
Each site is therefore BOTH a candidate place to land the supply (a
`pads[]` entry) AND the place that sub-block's own current leaves the
rail (a `current_model.instances[]` entry). `klt power` snaps an
instance to the nearest node on each of its nets independently, so an
instance placed at a site's `vdd` label returns its current at the
nearest `vss` node to that same point -- which is where that
sub-block's ground current physically leaves. The droop this flow
reports per site is read at exactly those two attachment nodes.
RESISTANCE CORNERS
`nominal`, `pessimistic` and `optimistic` are the gf180mcuD techfile's
own three `variants` blocks -- see `adc_block.power-spec.json`'s
`_comment` for the full table and both PDK sources. They are declared
here rather than in the base spec because a corner is a choice about
how to read the PDK, not a property of the layout.
`counterfactual_poly_as_metal1` and `counterfactual_metal2_as_poly2`
are NOT PDK corners and are not offered as ones. The first is the
nominal corner with Poly2's sheet resistance replaced by Metal1's --
`how much of this droop is the poly?`. The second is the nominal
corner with METAL2's replaced by Poly2's -- `what would this geometry
do if issue #378's straps were still poly?`, i.e. the control on the
change itself. A case using either is labelled a counterfactual in its
own claim and its verdict is not
CURRENT MODELS
Measured, not assumed, and measured for THIS purpose: the deck is
`sim/adc-rail-current/`, which adds MIN/AVG `meas` lines to the
committed `sim/adc-power/` netlist and reads the three supply sources
that are ONE `vdd` net in `adc_block.gds` (`vddc` the comparator,
`vddd` the CDAC bottom-plate drivers, `vddt` the top-plate switch) over
one window spanning every input level. See that experiment's own
`testbench/tb.json` for the sign convention and for why the peak is the
peak of the SUM rather than the sum of the peaks.
PER-SITE ATTRIBUTION. `vddc` -> `COMPARATOR`, `vddt` -> `ADC_TOP_SW`,
and `vddd` split evenly between `ADC_DECODE_BANK_P` and
`ADC_DECODE_BANK_N`. That mapping is the deck's own: `Xsecmp` and the
`iseb` bias source are on `vddc`, `Xsetswp`/`Xsetswn` are on `vddt`,
and `Xsearrp`/`Xsearrn` -- the P-side and N-side bottom-plate driver
arrays, which are what the two decode banks ARE in the layout -- are
both on `vddd`. The even split between the two banks is a symmetry
assumption, and it is the differential structure's own symmetry: the
two banks are generated from the same code with the same weights.
WHAT THE MEASURED CURRENT IS A LOWER BOUND ON, restated from the
deck's own manifest so it travels with the verdict: the SAR sequencer
and output register are DR-0010 rung-1 ideal XSPICE primitives and draw
no current, and the deck's 2 ns maximum timestep averages any spike
shorter than itself. Both push the measured current DOWN, so every
droop number here is a lower bound on the droop this block will really
develop. That is the non-conservative direction, and it is why the
budget is not treated as met with margin to spare -- see
`layout/power/README.md`.
STATIC vs PEAK -- what each case is for
The budget DR-0034 sets is on the STATIC drop at the average current;
that is what `pvt_worst_average` cases grade. The `pvt_worst_peak` case
is included and reported, but it is an UPPER BOUND, not a prediction:
a purely resistive network with no charge storage in it, asked to
source a sub-nanosecond CDAC switching transient, reports a drop larger
than the supply. What that says is that the DC path alone cannot source
the peak, which is true of essentially every block and is what
decoupling is for. Its `budget_status` is recorded as a fail and the
record says plainly what that does and does not mean.
THE CONTROLS
Three, for the three ways a clean number could be a lie:
* `control.doubled-current` doubles every instance current and
asserts, via `expect.scales_case`, that EVERY site's combined droop
is exactly 2x the case it perturbs. A linear resistive network must
do that; a solve that had quietly stopped consuming the current
model, or that was reporting a cached/other network, cannot. This
is the liveness control the absence of a fail would otherwise need.
* `control.poly-as-metal1` replaces Poly2's sheet resistance with
Metal1's and asserts the droop collapses. It is the counterfactual
that attributes the result: if this case were close to the real
one, the poly risers would not be the story and issue #346's premise
would be wrong -- which, since issue #378 took the block-level
current off poly, is now nearly true: it moves the COMPARATOR
landing from 1.703 to 1.574 mV, ~8 % rather than the ~71 % it
attributed on the Poly2-strapped geometry.
* `control.metal2-as-poly2` is the control on issue #378 itself: the
CURRENT geometry with Metal2 given Poly2's sheet resistance. It
must return the ADC_DECODE_BANK_P landing to the pre-#378 verdict
(33.177 mV, FAIL, against the 33.552 mV that geometry measured),
or the improvement is coming from something other than the straps.
RE-BASELINED AT ISSUE #378 (block-level supply straps on Metal2)
`layout_sha256` and every `expect` figure below were re-derived
against the Metal2-strapped geometry (`501f3985...`, DR-0037). The
three block-level `vdd`/`vss` straps -- the comparator's own supply
corridor and both hops of the switch-cell bridge -- run on Metal2 with
one Via1 per trunk instead of on Poly2 with one Contact per trunk.
`vcm` was deliberately left on Poly2 (it is a reference, not a supply,
and draws no standing current in the model above).
WHAT MOVED: two verdicts. The landed-at-`ADC_DECODE_BANK_P` case at
the nominal corner goes 33.552 -> 13.227 mV and at the pessimistic
corner 58.552 -> 17.184 mV, both from FAIL to PASS, so all four
labelled landing sites now meet DR-0034 at both corners -- which is
the whole of what issue #378 asked for. Two cases were ADDED so that
claim is checked rather than inferred:
`pessimistic.ADC_DECODE_BANK_N` and `pessimistic.ADC_TOP_SW`, the two
site/corner combinations the committed set never ran.
WHAT DID NOT MOVE: the network's shape (`vdd` 476 nodes / 477 edges,
`vss` 610 / 613, one island each) -- 3 Metal2 and 8 Via1 edges per
rail replace the same count of Poly2 and Contact edges. The EM verdict
is still `pass_partial` at every average-current case, with 375
checked and 715 unchecked edges (was 353 / 737): every in-sub-block
terminal riser is still Poly2, and gf180mcuD publishes no
current-density limit for Poly2 or Contact, so `pass` is not reachable
by re-running. The peak-current case still fails, still as an upper
bound, and is still issue #379's question.
PREVIOUSLY RE-BASELINED AT ISSUE #356 (well taps + tie straps)
Kept as history: #356 re-derived the same fields against the tapped
geometry (`ae4e8964...`, DR-0035), which added 25 n-well taps routed
to `vdd` on Poly2 risers and strapped both `Pplus`-marked
substrate-tie rings into `vss`. Both rails' solved networks grew
(`vdd` 376 -> 476 nodes, `vss` 494 -> 610), every droop figure got
~1.6 % worse, and no verdict flipped -- the landed-at-
`ADC_DECODE_BANK_P` case still missed the budget (33.029 -> 33.552
mV), which is the finding issue #378 was filed on.

supply._comment: The pad is held at the ratified NOMINAL supply (README.md#target-specification, DR-0004). The droop this flow reports is a difference, and in a linear resistive network it does not depend on the pad voltage at all -- only the current does, and the current model below carries its own measured supply per corner. 3.3 V is used so the solved node voltages in each report read as a recognisable rail rather than as an abstraction.

budget.applies_to: vdd droop + vss bounce at any of the four labelled sub-block sites, static, at the worst-corner average current
budget._comment: 0.10 x the ratified +/-10 % supply window (2 x 0.10 x 3.3 V = 330 mV), per README.md#target-specification note [a]'s 'keep it a minority term' convention. Derivation, alternatives and consequences are in the record; this is only the number the cases are graded against.

nominal.source: gf180mcuD.tech `variants ()`; metals cross-checked against gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0__nom.tlef RESISTANCE RPERSQ

pessimistic.source: gf180mcuD.tech `variants (hrhc),(hrlc)` high-end corner; metals cross-checked against gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0__max.tlef RESISTANCE RPERSQ 0.104

optimistic.source: gf180mcuD.tech `variants (lrhc),(lrlc)` low-end corner; metals cross-checked against gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0__min.tlef RESISTANCE RPERSQ 0.076

counterfactual_poly_as_metal1.source: NOT A PDK CORNER. The nominal corner with Poly2's sheet resistance replaced by Metal1's -- the counterfactual `what if the risers were metal` used by control.poly-as-metal1.

counterfactual_metal2_as_poly2.source: NOT A PDK CORNER. The nominal corner with Metal2's sheet resistance replaced by Poly2's -- the counterfactual `what if the block-level straps were still poly` used by control.metal2-as-poly2, i.e. the geometry issue #378 replaced, priced on the geometry that replaced it.

pvt_worst_average.source: sim/adc-rail-current/records/20260923-002945-1cefe83.md -- the worst `i_vdd_avg_ua` point of the 27-point PVT grid
pvt_worst_average._comment: The three measured averages placed at their own sub-blocks, with i_cdac_avg split evenly between the two decode banks. They sum to the measured i_vdd_avg exactly (30.7246 + 9.06449 + 0.330955 = 40.12 uA), because an average IS additive across sources -- unlike the peak below.

pvt_worst_peak.source: sim/adc-rail-current/records/20260923-002945-1cefe83.md -- the worst `i_vdd_peak_ua` point of the 27-point PVT grid
pvt_worst_peak._comment: A peak is NOT additive: the deck measures i_vdd_peak_ua as the peak of the SUM (34383.9 uA), which is smaller than the sum of the three per-source peaks (39048.98 uA) because they do not peak at the same instant. Loading the three separate peaks would invent a worst case the deck never produces. The three per-source peaks are therefore scaled by 34383.9 / 39048.98 = 0.8805326029 so they sum to the measured peak-of-sum, preserving the attribution the deck measured while totalling what it measured. i_cdac_peak is split evenly between the two decode banks as above. This model drives the upper-bound case only.

seeded_double_average.source: SEEDED CONTROL, not a measurement: pvt_worst_average with every instance current doubled
seeded_double_average._comment: Exists so a clean verdict is shown to be live. A linear resistive network must return exactly twice the droop; `control.doubled-current` asserts that site by site.

cases.name: landed.ADC_DECODE_BANK_P
cases.claim: static droop at every labelled site when the parent lands this block's supply on the P-side decode bank's label

cases.name: landed.ADC_DECODE_BANK_N
cases.claim: static droop at every labelled site when the parent lands this block's supply on the N-side decode bank's label

cases.name: landed.ADC_TOP_SW
cases.claim: static droop at every labelled site when the parent lands this block's supply on the top-plate switch's label

cases.name: landed.COMPARATOR
cases.claim: static droop at every labelled site when the parent lands this block's supply on the comparator's label

cases.name: pessimistic.ADC_DECODE_BANK_P
cases.role: worst landing site x pessimistic resistance corner
cases.claim: the corner of the corner: the landing site with the largest nominal droop, re-solved at the PDK's high-resistance corner

cases.name: pessimistic.COMPARATOR
cases.role: best landing site x pessimistic resistance corner
cases.claim: whether the best landing site still meets the budget when the resistance corner goes against it -- the question that decides whether this geometry is usable as drawn

cases.name: pessimistic.ADC_DECODE_BANK_N
cases.role: every landing site x pessimistic resistance corner
cases.claim: the second decode bank's label at the PDK's high-resistance corner -- one of the four cases that together make the DR-0034 verdict a property of the block rather than of where a parent lands the supply (issue #378)

cases.name: pessimistic.ADC_TOP_SW
cases.role: every landing site x pessimistic resistance corner
cases.claim: the top-plate switch cell's label at the PDK's high-resistance corner -- one of the four cases that together make the DR-0034 verdict a property of the block rather than of where a parent lands the supply (issue #378)

cases.name: optimistic.COMPARATOR
cases.role: best landing site x optimistic resistance corner
cases.claim: the other end of the resistance spread, so the record states a range rather than a single corner

cases.name: peak-upper-bound.COMPARATOR
cases.claim: what a purely resistive network with no charge storage would develop if asked to source the measured switching peak as a DC current -- i.e. a statement that the DC path alone cannot source the peak, and a lower bound on the decoupling this block relies on and does not specify

cases.name: control.doubled-current
cases.claim: doubling every instance current must exactly double every site's combined droop; a solve that had stopped consuming the current model cannot do that

cases.name: control.poly-as-metal1
cases.claim: COUNTERFACTUAL, not evidence about the drawn layout: the same solve with Poly2 given Metal1's sheet resistance, so the record can say how much of the droop the poly stitching is actually responsible for

cases.name: control.metal2-as-poly2
cases.claim: COUNTERFACTUAL, not evidence about the drawn layout: the same solve with Metal2 given Poly2's sheet resistance, i.e. this geometry with issue #378's straps un-done. It is the control on the whole change -- if it did NOT return this case to the pre-#378 verdict, the improvement would be coming from something other than the straps
